description: Where every phase puts what it produces. Before this existed each phase invented a path - the analyst wrote docs/ba/<feature>/RTM.md, the UI phase named a contrast report with no path at all - so the matrix written by one phase was not always the one the next phase looked for. That is how a traceability matrix silently stops being maintained. One map, one owner per artifact, and a resolution rule that defers to whatever the repository already does.

order: If the repository already has a home for this kind of document, use it. A repo with docs/adr/ gets its ADRs there, not in docs/design/<slug>/adr/. A repo with a docs site (docusaurus, mkdocs, vitepress, sphinx) gets documents inside that site's content root so they are actually published.
Otherwise use the default path below.
Slug is the feature or change name in kebab-case, decided once at intake and recorded in .onestop/run.json so every phase resolves to the same directory.
Never create a second documentation root. If docs/ and doc/ and documentation/ all exist, use the one with the most recently modified file and say which you chose.
resolution.announce: Name every path written in the phase output block. An artifact the user cannot locate was not delivered.

docs.purpose: Durable, human-readable output that belongs to the product and is reviewed like code. Committed.
docs.audience: the team, now and in six months

run_state.purpose: Machine state and run evidence for this orchestration. Gitignored - it is the orchestrator's working memory, not a product artifact.
run_state.audience: the orchestrator, and the user auditing what happened

code.purpose: Test and automation code, which is source and lives where the repo's source lives - never under docs/.

artifacts.what: Run state: intent, size tier, slug, phase list, per-phase status, gate decisions. The resume point.

Detected stack, bound language and concern packs, bound architecture pattern, bound automation frameworks and their patterns, bound runners. Written once, read by every later phase instead of re-detecting.
Append-only human-readable log: one line per phase started, per agent dispatched, per gate shown and answered. This is what makes a run auditable after the fact.
Objective, stakeholders, scope and explicit out-of-scope, domain model, process flows, functional and non-functional requirements.
Stories with testable acceptance criteria, each carrying its requirement id.
Requirements traceability matrix. Columns: Req-Id, Requirement, Source, Story, Impl-Ref, Test-Ref, Status.
The same matrix, importable into a tracker. Kept in step with the markdown - if they disagree, both are wrong.

filled_later.value: path:line of the code that satisfies the requirement
test id or spec path; a requirement may carry both a unit and an end-to-end reference

artifacts.what: What was looked up, from which source and version, and what it means for this change. Dated, because library guidance expires.
Found / gaps / options with file-level evidence, per flow step. Run state rather than product documentation - it describes the repo at one moment and goes stale immediately.
The system design: component diagram, the bound architecture pattern and why, data model, sequence for the primary flow, failure modes, scaling and security posture, and the trade-offs considered.
One decision per file, numbered, using templates/adr.md. Written only for decisions that are expensive to reverse.

artifacts.format: openapi | graphql | proto | asyncapi | typed interface
artifacts.what: The interface contract, written by contract-agent before either side is implemented. This is the artifact that unlocks parallel implementation.
The domain-matched OKLCH palette with measured contrast ratios per pair - measured, never estimated.
Design tokens as custom properties: colour, spacing, type scale, radius, elevation, motion. Light and dark. This is the file components import; the markdown explains it.
Component inventory with every interactive state specified - rest, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading, error, empty.

by_phase.note: If the repo already has a design system, extend it in place and write no new token file. Two token sources is the failure mode this phase exists to prevent.

artifacts.what: The ordered task list of thin vertical slices - each with acceptance criteria, the files it touches, and the test level that proves it. This is the artifact approved at Gate 1.
The execution DAG with declared write surfaces per task, grouped into waves. Produced by work-partitioner; consumed by parallel-execution.
The project structure for the bound architecture pattern - directories, entry point, config, a runnable empty app, and the test harness proven to run. No feature code.
Setup and run instructions that actually work from a clean clone. Verified by following them, not by writing them.
Every key the scaffold needs, with a placeholder value and a one-line comment.

by_phase.note: Produces no durable artifact by design - its output is a green suite, reported in the phase output block with the exact command and result. If it cannot get green, the blocker is named there rather than written to a file nobody will read.

artifacts.what: Application code, written to the bound architecture pattern with declared file roles.
Updated in place - Impl-Ref and Status filled for every requirement a completed slice satisfies.
Unit and integration tests beside the code they cover, following the repo's existing test location.
Test-Ref filled.
Web end-to-end suite, structured per the bound automation pattern - for fixture-composed page objects that means tests/, pages/, fixtures/, data/, support/ beneath this root.
App end-to-end suite - screens or robots, flows, data - per the bound pattern for the bound framework.
How to run each suite, which journeys are covered, which are not and why, and anything quarantined with the condition that would release it.
CI wiring - the suite on pull requests, artifacts uploaded on failure. Extend the existing workflow rather than adding a second one.
Manual plan: environment setup, concrete test-data creation steps, step-by-step cases with observable expected results, regression checklist, sign-off.
The same cases, importable into a test management tool.
Findings by severity with file:line, which reviewer raised each, and the disposition - fixed, accepted with reason, or deferred with an owner. Run evidence, not product documentation.
Which regime applies, which controls this change touches, and the evidence for each. Committed - this one is product documentation, because an auditor will ask for it.
Baseline before, measurement method, profile findings, result after, and the regression guard that keeps it. A performance claim without a before number is not a claim.
The failing regression test that reproduces the defect. It is the first artifact of a defect run and it is committed with the fix.
Updated only where the change actually invalidated it - new commands, new env vars, changed setup.
One entry describing the user-visible change.
An entry for every new key. A key that exists in .env and not here breaks the next person's clone.
What the gate showed - progress, just did, next, remaining, recommendation, options - and what the user chose. Written when the gate is answered, so a resumed run knows what was already agreed.

never: Never write a document into the application source tree. src/ is code; docs/ is documentation. A design document under src/ is invisible to everyone who reads documentation and noise to everyone who reads code.
Never put test or automation code under docs/. It is source, it must be runnable, and it belongs where the runner looks for it.
Never create a parallel documentation root when one exists. Detect first.
Never commit .onestop/ run state. It is working memory - ensure the gitignore entry exists before the first write.
Never write an artifact and fail to name its path in the phase output. An unnamed artifact is one the user will not find and will not read.
